body: BSE Smallcap record high 20,183 on 15 Jan 2018 (Business Standard; another BS piece cites 18,672 on 14 Feb 2018 as the 52-week high - definitions differ); -23.5% in calendar 2018; ~-40% from Jan 2018 to Aug 2019 (Value Research). Smallcap 250 TRI -36% vs Nifty 50 TRI -14% (DSP drawdown table); intra-year fall of the Smallcap 100 ~40%. Meanwhile the Nifty kept making highs into Aug-Sept 2018 - a narrow market. Triggers: Oct 2017 SEBI MF recategorisation (fixed definitions of large/mid/small caps forced portfolio reshuffles), Feb 2018 budget reintroducing LTCG tax, the ASM surveillance framework (2018), the IL&FS default (Sept 2018; ~Rs 91,000 crore of debt, from memory), DHFL's ~60% intraday crash (21 Sept 2018) and an NBFC funding freeze; then 2019 governance blow-ups (DHFL, Yes Bank, Cox & Kings, CG Power). Leaders before: everything small, MF-flow beneficiaries; laggards: NBFCs/housing finance, autos, realty, promoter-pledged names. Winners during: large private banks, IT, consumer 'quality' (the 2019-20 quality premium peak). Recovery: ~3 years to regain the prior peak (DSP) - aided by the 2020 liquidity wave. Top signals: record SIP and small-cap fund inflows, breadth peaking (Jan 2018) while the index rose, IPO and QIP rush by small companies. Lesson: breadth divergence plus a credit event = small-cap bear market even if the Nifty looks fine.
title: 2018-19 smallcap crash and IL&FS/NBFC freeze
